Saint Makarios of Corinth

St. Makarios Notaras · St. Macarius of Corinth · St. Makarius of Corinth · St. Macarios of Corinth · St. Michael Notaras

Period
1731–1805
Region
Corinth; Mount Athos; Patmos; Chios, Greece
Titles / vocation
Hierarch · Teacher
Commemoration
April 17

Introduction

Saint Makarios was Archbishop of Corinth and a monastic teacher associated with Saint Nikodemos the Hagiorite and the publication of the Philokalia.

Read the published life [1]

BackgroundLife and notable eventsDeath and martyrdomWritings and legacyChronology
Death / martyrdom

Repose on Chios in 1805; not described as a martyr

Read circumstances and sources

Background

Born at Trikala in Corinth in 1731, he belonged to the Notaras family and was baptized Michael. He taught young people in Corinth without payment before becoming its archbishop in 1764.

[1] Published ecclesiastical biography / commemoration · Opening paragraphs: family, baptismal name and teaching

Life and notable events

War forced him away from Corinth, and another archbishop was appointed. He later visited Mount Athos, where disputes over memorial services affected monastic life. He founded a settlement on Patmos and eventually lived on Chios, teaching, hearing confessions, and assisting people in need.

[1] Published ecclesiastical biography / commemoration · Paragraphs on exile, Athos, Patmos and residence on Chios

Death and martyrdom

Saint Makarios died on April 17, 1805. He was buried beside the church of the Holy Apostles Sts. Peter and Paul on Chios. His relics were recovered in 1808. This account does not describe martyrdom.

[1] Published ecclesiastical biography / commemoration · Final biographical paragraph: repose, burial, recovery of relics

Writings and legacy

He helped secure support for publishing the Philokalia and the catechism of Metropolitan Platon of Moscow. His collaboration with Saint Nikodemos links his episcopal ministry with the transmission of older Orthodox spiritual writings.

[1] Published ecclesiastical biography / commemoration · Paragraphs on funding publications and work with Saint Nikodemos
